questions.prompt: A UserService class validates input, hashes passwords, writes to the database and sends welcome emails. A change to the email template forces you to retest the database code. Which principle is most directly violated?
options: Liskov substitution
Single responsibility
Interface segregation
Open/closed
questions.explanation: The class has several reasons to change (validation, persistence, email), so unrelated edits ripple through it. Splitting it by responsibility isolates each change.

questions.prompt: ReadOnlyList subclasses List and raises an exception from append(). Code that accepts any List now crashes when given a ReadOnlyList. What is the best fix?
options: Catch the exception at every call site
Add an is_read_only flag checked before append()
Make ReadOnlyList a separate type that List extends
Override append() to silently do nothing
questions.explanation: A subtype that refuses base-class operations breaks Liskov substitution. Invert the hierarchy: a read-only base with a mutable subtype keeps every promise; silently ignoring append() just hides the broken contract.

questions.prompt: ReportGenerator does self.db = PostgresDatabase() in its constructor, so unit tests need a live database. Which change applies dependency inversion?
options: Make PostgresDatabase a singleton
Pass any object with a query() method into the constructor
Subclass ReportGenerator for each test
Move the connection string to an environment variable
questions.explanation: Depending on an abstraction (anything with query()) that is passed in lets tests inject a fake. A singleton or env var still hard-wires the concrete database.

questions.prompt: Your tests pass one at a time but fail when run together, because a Config singleton keeps values set by earlier tests. What is the cleanest long-term fix?
options: Run every test in its own process
Add a reset() method called at the start of each test
Create one Config in main() and inject it where needed
Make the singleton thread-safe with a lock
questions.explanation: The root problem is hidden global state. Creating the object once and passing it in makes each test build its own Config; reset() only patches the symptom.

questions.prompt: An HTTP client has 12 optional settings (timeouts, retries, headers, proxy, TLS options) and some combinations are invalid. Which creational approach fits best?
options: Builder (or keyword arguments) that validates in build()
Prototype cloned from a default client
Abstract Factory with one factory per setting
Singleton client shared by the whole app
questions.explanation: Builder exists for objects with many optional parts and a final validation step. In Python, keyword-only arguments plus validation in __post_init__ often give the same benefit.

questions.prompt: You cloned a template game level with copy.copy(), changed the clone's enemies list, and the template's enemies changed too. Why?
options: copy.copy() only copies immutable attributes
Lists cannot be copied in Python
Prototype objects are always shared by reference
A shallow copy shares nested mutable objects like the list
questions.explanation: copy.copy() creates a new outer object but its attributes still point to the same list. copy.deepcopy() recursively copies nested objects.

questions.prompt: Your app calls storage.save(key, bytes). A new cloud SDK only offers put_object(Bucket=..., Key=..., Body=...). You want no changes in the app code. Which pattern fits?
options: Decorator
Composite
Adapter
Bridge
questions.explanation: An adapter translates one interface into the one callers expect, keeping behavior the same. A decorator keeps the same interface and adds behavior.

questions.prompt: You need logging, caching and retries in any combination around an API client, without writing a subclass for each of the 7 non-empty combinations. What do you use?
options: Decorators that wrap the client with the same interface
A facade that exposes one method per combination
A proxy that blocks unauthenticated calls
A composite tree of API clients
questions.explanation: Decorators share the wrapped object's interface, so they stack in any order and combination: Retry(Cache(Log(client))).

questions.prompt: You have 4 notification types (alert, reminder, digest, promo) and 3 channels (email, SMS, push). Subclassing every pair gives 12 classes. Which pattern reduces this, and to how many classes?
options: Facade, to 1 class
Composite, to 4 classes
Bridge, to 7 classes
Adapter, to 3 classes
questions.explanation: Bridge separates the two dimensions: notifications hold a channel, so you write 4 + 3 = 7 classes instead of 4 x 3 = 12.

questions.prompt: A text editor needs undo/redo for typing, deleting and formatting. Which pattern is the natural fit?
options: Observer
Command
Iterator
Template Method
questions.explanation: Each edit becomes an object with execute() and undo() kept on a history stack, which is exactly what Command provides.

questions.prompt: A Document class has publish(), edit() and archive(), each containing the same if/elif over draft, review, published and archived. Adding a status means editing every method. Which refactor helps most?
options: Strategy chosen by the caller for each call
Observer that broadcasts status changes
Chain of Responsibility over the methods
State: one class per status that the Document delegates to
questions.explanation: When behavior depends on the object's own changing status, State moves each branch into a status class and lets transitions replace the repeated conditionals.

questions.prompt: A web framework runs every request through auth, rate limiting and input validation; any step may reject the request with an error, otherwise it continues. Which pattern describes this?
options: Chain of Responsibility
Template Method
Composite
Strategy
questions.explanation: Middleware is a chain: each handler either handles or stops the request, or forwards it to the next link.

questions.prompt: You want to restructure a 400-line legacy function that has no tests. What should you do first?
options: Rewrite it from scratch in a cleaner style
Write characterization tests that pin its current behavior
Split it into files, then add tests later
Add comments explaining each block
questions.explanation: Refactoring must preserve behavior, and you cannot prove that without tests. Characterization tests record what the code does today, bugs included, so every small step can be checked.

questions.prompt: Two functions in different modules contain nearly identical 10-line blocks, but one follows tax law and the other follows marketing rules, and they change at different times. What is the best call?
options: Merge them into one shared helper immediately
Delete one and call the other from both modules
Keep them separate; they look alike but change for different reasons
Move both into a base class
questions.explanation: DRY is about one source of truth per piece of knowledge, not about identical-looking text. Merging code with different reasons to change creates coupling and flag-ridden helpers.

questions.prompt: A function computes a cutoff with time.time() - 86400 * 30 inside its body, and its tests are flaky near midnight. Which pair of fixes addresses both problems?
options: Inject the clock and replace 86400 with a named constant
Add more comments and a retry loop in the test
Cache the result and use a global variable
Convert the function into a singleton class
questions.explanation: Injecting the time source makes tests deterministic, and a named constant like SECONDS_PER_DAY removes the magic number smell.
